addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- amazon-bedrock: Builds generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore. Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.
- aws-billing-and-cost-management: Analyze AWS costs, find savings, manage budgets, evaluate Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, right-size EC2/Lambda/RDS/EBS with Compute Optimizer, look up service pricing, query CUR with Athena, detect cost anomalies, scope costs to billing views, and monitor Free Tier usage. Triggers on: AWS bill, cost analysis, reduce spend, savings plan, reserved instance, right-size, budget alert, cost optimization, pricing, free tier, cost anomaly, CUR, cost audit, billing view, billing view ARN.

Applies when creating APIs, selecting Building Blocks (KVStore, DistributedTable, Database, AuthBasic, AuthCognito, Realtime, AsyncJob, FileBucket, etc.), running local development, or deploying AWS Blocks applications. Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.
- aws-cdk: Authors, deploys, and troubleshoots AWS infrastructure using CDK with TypeScript or Python. Covers best practices, stack architecture, and construct patterns. Always use when writing CDK constructs, bootstrapping environments, running cdk deploy/synth/diff, fixing CDK or CloudFormation errors, planning stack structure, importing existing resources, resolving drift, or refactoring stacks without resource replacement.
- aws-cloudformation: Author, validate, and troubleshoot AWS CloudFormation templates. Covers template authoring with secure defaults, pre-deployment validation (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, change sets), and root-cause diagnosis of failed stacks using CloudFormation events and CloudTrail correlation.
- aws-containers: Deploys and operates containerized workloads on ECS, Fargate, and ECR. Covers task definitions, Fargate services, ECR repository setup and lifecycle policies, ECS Exec debugging, service scaling, deployment strategies, load balancer integration, and logging configuration. Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.
- aws-messaging-and-streaming: Guides use of AWS messaging and streaming services. Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.
- aws-observability: Builds, configures, debugs, and optimizes AWS observability with CloudWatch (Log Insights, Metrics, Alarms, Dashboards, EMF), X-Ray, CloudTrail, and ADOT (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry), AND enables/onboards services to Application Signals using ADOT auto-instrumentation SDKs. Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Covers cold starts, CORS debugging, event source mappings, troubleshooting, concurrency, SnapStart, Powertools, function URLs, EventBridge Scheduler, Lambda layers, and production readiness. Triggers on mentions of Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, SAM templates, CDK serverless stacks, DynamoDB stream triggers, SQS event sources, cold starts, timeouts, 502/504 errors, throttling, concurrency, CORS, Powertools, or any event-driven architecture on AWS, even without the word "serverless." - cso: Chief Security Officer mode. (gstack)

This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

- review: Pre-landing PR review. (gstack)

Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. content.text: I'll read redu.md first.

content.content:
1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/asciinema/asciinema-server
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: ghcr.io/asciinema/asciinema-server:20260626
7	  port: 4000
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: asciinema
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔⛔ THE ADMIN PANEL ON PORT 4002 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL, AND THE PUBLISHED IMAGE BINDS IT TO EVERY INTERFACE. Upstream's own documentation says the dedicated admin endpoint performs no authentication and that anyone who can reach port 4002 has full admin access, and it says the port is bound to localhost by default. In the release image it is NOT: Dockerfile:79 sets ADMIN_BIND_ALL=1, which config/runtime.exs:86-88 turns into a 0.0.0.0 bind, overriding the 127.0.0.1 default in config/prod.exs:22. The only thing between the internet and full administrative control of the instance is that you did not publish that port. So: map ONLY 4000 in the compose, never add 4002 to the ports list, never pass 4002 to deploy_compose, and never open it in a security group. If the user wants the panel, set ADMIN_PANEL_ON_MAIN_ENDPOINT=1, which serves it at /admin behind a login and answers 404 to logged-in users without the admin flag."
18	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO REGISTER, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. lib/asciinema/accounts.ex:351-358 inserts the first user that has an email with is_admin true, and logs 'granted admin to first registered user #N'. There is no install wizard, no setup token and no deploy-time admin account. The window is open from the moment the hostname resolves until somebody claims it, and on this app the claim is a two-step passwordless flow, so it takes longer than usual. Claim it AS PART OF THE DEPLOY, before the URL is handed to anyone: open /login, enter the user's email, then read the sign-in link out of the container log as described in the next quirk."
19	  - "⛔ WITHOUT SMTP, EVERY LOGIN LINK IS IN THE CONTAINER LOG, AND THAT IS THE DOCUMENTED WAY TO BOOTSTRAP. asciinema has no passwords at all: you enter an email address and it sends a short-lived one-time link. lib/asciinema/emails.ex:43-53 shows that with no SMTP configured the mailer falls back to a local adapter that logs every link as 'url from email: <url>'. So run `sudo docker logs <container> | grep 'url from email'`, take the LAST one (they are single-use and expire in about an hour), and open it. The first link's path is /users/new?t=... (sign-up, where you pick a username); later ones are /session/new?t=.... Say this out loud at handover, because it has a consequence: with no SMTP, EVERY future login by EVERY user needs someone with shell access to the VM. That is fine for a single-user instance and unworkable for a shared one, so a multi-user instance needs the SMTP_* variables (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT default 587, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD) pointed at a relay the user already owns."
20	  - "⛔ SET SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true AFTER YOU HAVE CLAIMED THE ADMIN ACCOUNT, NEVER BEFORE. It disables public signups and allows login for existing users only, which is exactly what a personal instance wants. Set it on a database with no users and there is no supported way left to create the first one: the escape hatch upstream documents for that situation is the unauthenticated admin port, which is the one thing this recipe refuses to expose. The order is deploy, claim, then redeploy with SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true."
21	  - "⛔⛔ ANONYMOUS UPLOADS ARE ACCEPTED BY DEFAULT, WHICH ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS AN OPEN WRITE ENDPOINT. lib/asciinema/accounts.ex:678-693: when upload_auth_required is false, and config/runtime.exs:275-276 shows false is the default, an unrecognised CLI install id makes the server CREATE A TEMPORARY USER and accept the recording. POST /api/asciicasts is routed with no authentication plug in front of it (lib/asciinema_web/router.ex:136). Upstream is explicit that this is meant for trusted LANs. On redu the hostname is public, so set UPLOAD_AUTH_REQUIRED=true, and set UNREGISTERED_UPLOAD_COUNT_LIMIT=0 as well if you want unregistered CLIs blocked outright rather than merely unknown ones. Leaving it open means strangers filling the app VM's disk with recordings you are paying to store."
22	  - "⛔ SET SECRET_KEY_BASE OR EVERY RESTART SIGNS EVERYONE OUT. rel/overlays/bin/server:22-30: when it is unset the entrypoint GENERATES a random 64-character value for that boot and prints only a '[warning]' line, then carries on. Nothing errors, nothing is lost from the database, and every session cookie, including yours, becomes invalid at the next container restart. On an instance whose only login mechanism is a one-time link from the log, that is more annoying than it sounds. Generate 64 or more random alphanumeric characters, pass them at the first deploy, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy. It also keys other cryptographic operations (config/runtime.exs:44-48 feeds it to both endpoints and to Accounts), so treat it as permanent."
23	  - "⛔⛔ THE IMAGE BAKES A DATABASE_URL POINTING AT A CONTAINER CALLED postgres, AND THAT IS THIS APP'S SILENT-FALLBACK TRAP. Dockerfile:80 sets DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@postgres/postgres. There is no SQLite path here, so a MISSING database is loud (the app cannot start), but the dangerous case is different: if you copy upstream's compose template and leave its bundled `postgres` service in place, the baked-in URL resolves to it, everything comes up healthy, and every recording, account and API token lands in a container-local database that dies with the app VM while the managed Postgres you are paying for stays empty. DELETE the bundled postgres service and set DATABASE_URL explicitly to the managed one. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS the PG variables to the project .env; it never edits your compose, so the mapping is yours to write."
24	  - "⛔ PROVE WHICH DATABASE IT LANDED IN, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A green page proves nothing. POSITIVE, and run it first because it also proves your exec command works at all: `sudo docker exec <container> printenv DATABASE_URL` must print the managed host, not the string 'postgres@postgres'. POSITIVE, and this is the one that settles it: connect to the managed Postgres and confirm asciinema's tables exist (users, asciicasts and schema_migrations are created by the automatic migration at boot). CORROBORATING: `sudo docker logs <container> | grep -c 'Running database migrations'` must be at least 1. If the table query comes back empty while the site works, you are looking at a second database inside the compose stack."
25	  - "PERCENT-ENCODE THE PASSWORD IN DATABASE_URL, BECAUSE THERE IS NO SEPARATE PASSWORD VARIABLE. The whole connection is one URI, postgresql://user:[REDACTED:conn-password]@host:port/dbname, parsed as a URI, so any @ : / ? # or % in redu's generated password must be percent-encoded or the URL parses into the wrong host and the error will not point at the password. Two query parameters are worth setting: ?ssl=true, which is OFF by default and costs nothing over redu's private network, and &pool_size=N (default 10) if you are tuning. asciinema uses exactly ONE database and creates no second one, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites, and no db_superuser is needed: 102 migrations were checked and not one of them creates an extension."
26	  - "⛔ THE RECORDINGS ARE FILES, THE DATABASE ONLY HOLDS METADATA, AND THEY DO NOT HAVE THE SAME LIFETIME ON redu. rel/env.sh.eex sets DATA_DIR to /var/lib/asciinema and config/runtime.exs:108-110 puts the local file store at ${DATA_DIR}/uploads, so every .cast file lives on the app VM. Mount a volume on /var/lib/asciinema or they vanish on the next redeploy while the rows describing them survive, which leaves a library full of recordings that will not play. Even with the volume, deleting the deployment destroys the files while the managed Postgres keeps the metadata: say that plainly before anyone deletes anything. If the user wants the recordings to outlive the VM, the supported answer is the S3-compatible file store (S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) pointed at a bucket they own."
27	  - "⛔ PIN 20260626 WITHOUT THE v, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE GITHUB RELEASE PAGE SUGGESTS. Measured against the ghcr.io API on 2026-08-17: a manifest request for ghcr.io/asciinema/asciinema-server:20260626 answers 200 and the same request for :v20260626 answers 404, while the GitHub release itself is named v20260626. Releases are date-stamped rather than semver, so the tag IS the date. There is also a rolling `canary` tag built from the development branch, which must never appear in a recipe. The image is published only to ghcr.io, not to Docker Hub."
28	  - "URL_HOST AND URL_SCHEME MUST BE RIGHT AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT AFTERWARDS. They build every generated link and the live-streaming WebSocket URL, and URL_HOST defaults to localhost. Generate the dname yourself in full `asciinema-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known before the container starts, then set URL_HOST to it and URL_SCHEME=https. Leave URL_PORT UNSET: config/runtime.exs:74-81 makes URL_SCHEME=https imply port 443, and setting URL_PORT is only for non-standard public ports. Upstream's own troubleshooting note is that if uploads work but live streams show as offline, these values are the first thing to check. Note that live streaming also needs the edge to pass WebSocket upgrades through to /ws/; the recording and playback path does not, so an instance can be perfectly useful before that is confirmed."
29	  - "PORT 4000, AND THERE IS NO HEALTH ENDPOINT. Dockerfile:78 sets PORT=4000 and config/prod.exs:12-18 binds the main endpoint on every interface, so no BIND_ALL is needed (that flag exists, but the prod default is already 0.0.0.0). Pass 4000 to deploy_compose. There is no /health or /status route in lib/asciinema_web/router.ex: probe GET /, which is the Explore page and answers to anonymous visitors. The page carries the asciinema branding and a link to /about, which is what a verification script should look for rather than a status code alone."
30	  - "NO migrate_command. rel/overlays/bin/server:32-35 runs ./migrate before starting the server, on EVERY boot, so a fresh managed Postgres is populated on first start and an upgrade applies its migrations automatically. That is also why the upgrade path is just a new image tag. Read upstream's upgrading page before jumping several releases at once."
31	  - "⛔ DO NOT ADAPT dev/docker-compose.yml. It is the developer stack: it builds from Dockerfile.dev, mounts the whole source tree at /app with named volumes for _build, deps and node_modules, runs `mix phx.server` under MIX_ENV unset, and puts an nginx container in front. None of that belongs on a server. The template worth copying is the one on upstream's quick-start page, minus its bundled postgres (you have a managed one) and minus its caddy container (redu terminates TLS at the edge; a second ACME client fighting for ports 80 and 443 is a real problem, not a cosmetic one)."
32	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS VISITOR CAN REACH, ONCE THE ABOVE IS SET: the Explore page at /, the sign-in page, /about, and any recording whose visibility is public. DEFAULT_RECORDING_VISIBILITY defaults to unlisted, so new uploads are link-only rather than listed, and it accepts public, unlisted or private if the user wants a different default. Live streaming is enabled for all users by default (DEFAULT_STREAMING_ENABLED=false turns it off for NEW users only; existing ones must be changed individually in the admin panel). UPLOAD_SIZE_LIMIT is 8 MB per recording unless raised."
33	  - "SIZING: UPSTREAM PUBLISHES A FIGURE AND THIS IS IT, NOT A redu MEASUREMENT. The self-hosting page states 512 MB of RAM minimum for a personal instance and 1 GB recommended for a community or company instance. m1.small gives 2 GB, which clears the recommended figure with room for Ubuntu and dockerd, and this is a BEAM release rather than a build, so nothing compiles on the VM. Reach for m1.medium if the instance is genuinely multi-user, or if the recordings will outgrow m1.small's 20 GB of flavor disk (m1.medium has 40 GB); growing that later is a volume resize, not a redeploy. Measure the real figure on the first run and write it back here."
34	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate the dname up front -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 4000 -> claim the admin account from the log link IMMEDIATELY -> then redeploy with SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true."
35	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built: the image is pulled. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."

46	the browser at real resolution, share them by link, and stream a live terminal session. Same
47	software that runs asciinema.org, on infrastructure you control.

54	- **asciinema server** from the official image, pinned to `20260626`, on one m1.small VM, port
55	  4000.
56	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding accounts and recording metadata.

69	## One decision to make before you deploy
70	
71	**Is there an SMTP relay, or not?** asciinema has no passwords: you type an email address and it
72	sends a one-time sign-in link.
73	
74	- **No SMTP** is fully supported and is what a single-user instance wants. Every link is written
75	  to the container log instead, so signing in means `sudo docker logs <container> | grep 'url from
76	  email'`. That is fine for one person with shell access and unworkable for a team.
77	- **With SMTP** (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, port defaults to 587), links
78	  arrive by email and the instance can have real users.

87	Map 4000 and nothing else, and use `ADMIN_PANEL_ON_MAIN_ENDPOINT=1` to get a login-gated panel at

91	during the deploy, then close signups with `SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true`, in that order.

96

98	upstream's bundled database service and everything works beautifully in a container-local Postgres

106	#!/usr/bin/env bash

108	set -u
109	: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname}"

112	code=$(curl -sSL -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/")

116	  echo "still starting. This one boots a BEAM release and runs its migrations first, so give it"

139	  *)       echo "WARNING: anonymous POST /api/asciicasts answered $up rather than 401 or 403."

141	           echo "Set UPLOAD_AUTH_REQUIRED=true and redeploy before publishing this URL." ;;

147	echo "     It must name the managed host, not 'postgres@postgres'. Then list asciinema's tables"

  vm: m1.small

  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp

  - "⛔⛔⛔ THE ADMIN PANEL ON PORT 4002 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL, AND THE PUBLISHED IMAGE BINDS IT TO EVERY INTERFACE. The only thing between the internet and full administrative control of the instance is that you did not publish that port. So: map ONLY 4000 in the compose, never add 4002 to the ports list, never pass 4002 to deploy_compose, and never open it in a security group. If the user wants the panel, set ADMIN_PANEL_ON_MAIN_ENDPOINT=1, which serves it at /admin behind a login and answers 404 to logged-in users without the admin flag."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO REGISTER, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. lib/asciinema/accounts.ex:351-358 inserts the first user that has an email with is_admin true, and logs 'granted admin to first registered user #N'. There is no install wizard, no setup token and no deploy-time admin account. The window is open from the moment the hostname resolves until somebody claims it, and on this app the claim is a two-step passwordless flow, so it takes longer than usual. Claim it AS PART OF THE DEPLOY, before the URL is handed to anyone: open /login, enter the user's email, then read the sign-in link out of the container log as described in the next quirk."
  - "⛔ WITHOUT SMTP, EVERY LOGIN LINK IS IN THE CONTAINER LOG, AND THAT IS THE DOCUMENTED WAY TO BOOTSTRAP. asciinema has no passwords at all: you enter an email address and it sends a short-lived one-time link. lib/asciinema/emails.ex:43-53 shows that with no SMTP configured the mailer falls back to a local adapter that logs every link as 'url from email: <url>'.   - "⛔ SET SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true AFTER YOU HAVE CLAIMED THE ADMIN ACCOUNT, NEVER BEFORE.   - "⛔⛔ ANONYMOUS UPLOADS ARE ACCEPTED BY DEFAULT, WHICH ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS AN OPEN WRITE ENDPOINT. lib/asciinema/accounts.ex:678-693: when upload_auth_required is false, and config/runtime.exs:275-276 shows false is the default, an unrecognised CLI install id makes the server CREATE A TEMPORARY USER and accept the recording.   - "⛔ SET SECRET_KEY_BASE OR EVERY RESTART SIGNS EVERYONE OUT. rel/overlays/bin/server:22-30: when it is unset the entrypoint GENERATES a random 64-character value for that boot and prints only a '[warning]' line, then carries on. Nothing errors, nothing is lost from the database, and every session cookie, including yours, becomes invalid at the next container restart. On an instance whose only login mechanism is a one-time link from the log, that is more annoying than it sounds. Generate 64 or more random alphanumeric characters, pass them at the first deploy, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy.   - "⛔⛔ THE IMAGE BAKES A DATABASE_URL POINTING AT A CONTAINER CALLED postgres, AND THAT IS THIS APP'S SILENT-FALLBACK TRAP. Dockerfile:80 sets DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@postgres/postgres.   - "⛔ PROVE WHICH DATABASE IT LANDED IN, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A green page proves nothing. POSITIVE, and run it first because it also proves your exec command works at all: `sudo docker exec <container> printenv DATABASE_URL` must print the managed host, not the string 'postgres@postgres'. POSITIVE, and this is the one that settles it: connect to the managed Postgres and confirm asciinema's tables exist (users, asciicasts and schema_migrations are created by the automatic migration at boot). CORROBORATING: `sudo docker logs <container> | grep -c 'Running database migrations'` must be at least 1. If the table query comes back empty while the site works, you are looking at a second database inside the compose stack."
  - "PERCENT-ENCODE THE PASSWORD IN DATABASE_URL, BECAUSE THERE IS NO SEPARATE PASSWORD VARIABLE. The whole connection is one URI, postgresql://user:[REDACTED:conn-password]@host:port/dbname, parsed as a URI, so any @ : / ? # or % in redu's generated password must be percent-encoded or the URL parses into the wrong host and the error will not point at the password.   - "⛔ THE RECORDINGS ARE FILES, THE DATABASE ONLY HOLDS METADATA, AND THEY DO NOT HAVE THE SAME LIFETIME ON redu. rel/env.sh.eex sets DATA_DIR to /var/lib/asciinema and config/runtime.exs:108-110 puts the local file store at ${DATA_DIR}/uploads, so every .cast file lives on the app VM. Mount a volume on /var/lib/asciinema or they vanish on the next redeploy while the rows describing them survive, which leaves a library full of recordings that will not play. Even with the volume, deleting the deployment destroys the files while the managed Postgres keeps the metadata: say that plainly before anyone deletes anything. If the user wants the recordings to outlive the VM, the supported answer is the S3-compatible file store (S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) pointed at a bucket they own."
  - "⛔ PIN 20260626 WITHOUT THE v, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE GITHUB RELEASE PAGE SUGGESTS. Measured against the ghcr.io API on 2026-08-17: a manifest request for ghcr.io/asciinema/asciinema-server:20260626 answers 200 and the same request for :v20260626 answers 404, while the GitHub release itself is named v20260626. Releases are date-stamped rather than semver, so the tag IS the date. There is also a rolling `canary` tag built from the development branch, which must never appear in a recipe. The image is published only to ghcr.io, not to Docker Hub."
  - "URL_HOST AND URL_SCHEME MUST BE RIGHT AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT AFTERWARDS. They build every generated link and the live-streaming WebSocket URL, and URL_HOST defaults to localhost. Generate the dname yourself in full `asciinema-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known before the container starts, then set URL_HOST to it and URL_SCHEME=https. Leave URL_PORT UNSET: config/runtime.exs:74-81 makes URL_SCHEME=https imply port 443, and setting URL_PORT is only for non-standard public ports. Upstream's own troubleshooting note is that if uploads work but live streams show as offline, these values are the first thing to check. Note that live streaming also needs the edge to pass WebSocket upgrades through to /ws/; the recording and playback path does not, so an instance can be perfectly useful before that is confirmed."
  - "PORT 4000, AND THERE IS NO HEALTH ENDPOINT. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# HOST=asciinema-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud ./verify.sh
set -u

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/")

if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ]; then

  echo "still starting. This one boots a BEAM release and runs its migrations first, so give it"
  echo "a couple of minutes and re-run rather than reading it as a failure."

fi
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "FAIL: / answered $code"; rm -f "$body"; exit 1; }

# the proxy. Every assertion below is meaningless without it.
if ! grep -qi 'asciinema' "$body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body does not mention asciinema at all."
  rm -f "$body"; exit 2
fi
rm -f "$body"

# The anonymous upload endpoint. A locked instance refuses it; an open one accepts a recording
# from a stranger. 401 or 403 is the PASS here.
up=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      "https://$HOST/api/asciicasts")
case "$up" in
  401|403) echo "OK: anonymous upload is refused (UPLOAD_AUTH_REQUIRED is on)" ;;
  404)     echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the upload route answered 404, so it has moved and this check"
           echo "proves nothing. Find the current route before trusting anything here."; exit 2 ;;
  *)       echo "WARNING: anonymous POST /api/asciicasts answered $up rather than 401 or 403."
           echo "On an open instance the server creates a temporary user and stores the upload."
           echo "Set UPLOAD_AUTH_REQUIRED=true and redeploy before publishing this URL." ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to confirm, and neither can be seen from out here:"
echo "  1. WHICH database. Run: sudo docker exec <container> printenv DATABASE_URL"
echo "     It must name the managed host, not 'postgres@postgres'. Then list asciinema's tables"
echo "     in the managed Postgres: users and asciicasts must be there."
echo "  2. That SECRET_KEY_BASE was set. sudo docker logs <container> | grep SECRET_KEY_BASE"
echo "     must print NOTHING; the warning line only appears when it was generated at boot."
echo "     Pair it with: printenv SECRET_KEY_BASE inside the container, which must be non-empty."
```

  - "THE ADMIN PANEL ON PORT 4002 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL, AND THE PUBLISHED IMAGE BINDS IT TO EVERY INTERFACE. If the user wants the panel, set ADMIN_PANEL_ON_MAIN_ENDPOINT=1, which serves it at /admin behind a login."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO REGISTER, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. Claim it AS PART OF THE DEPLOY, before the URL is handed to anyone: open /login, enter the user's email, then read the sign-in link out of the container log."
  - "WITHOUT SMTP, EVERY LOGIN LINK IS IN THE CONTAINER LOG. Run `sudo docker logs <container> | grep 'url from email'`, take the LAST one (single-use, expires in about an hour). First link path is /users/new?t=..., later ones /session/new?t=.... With no SMTP, EVERY future login by EVERY user needs shell access to the VM; a multi-user instance needs SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT (587), SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD."
  - "SET SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true AFTER YOU HAVE CLAIMED THE ADMIN ACCOUNT, NEVER BEFORE. Order is deploy, claim, then redeploy with SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true."

  - "THE IMAGE BAKES A DATABASE_URL POINTING AT A CONTAINER CALLED postgres. DELETE any bundled postgres service and set DATABASE_URL explicitly to the managed one. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS the PG variables to the project .env; it never edits your compose."

  - "PERCENT-ENCODE THE PASSWORD IN DATABASE_URL. The whole connection is one URI parsed as a URI. Worth setting ?ssl=true and &pool_size=N. asciinema uses exactly ONE database and needs no db_superuser."
  - "THE RECORDINGS ARE FILES, THE DATABASE ONLY HOLDS METADATA. DATA_DIR is /var/lib/asciinema and the local file store is ${DATA_DIR}/uploads. Mount a volume on /var/lib/asciinema.   - "PORT 4000, AND THERE IS NO HEALTH ENDPOINT. Pass 4000 to deploy_compose. Probe GET /, the Explore page, and look for the asciinema branding rather than a status code alone."
  - "NO migrate_command. The entrypoint runs ./migrate before starting the server on EVERY boot."

# Self-host asciinema server on redu

One Elixir container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. About GBP 0.035/hour,
roughly GBP 25 a month. Inside the no-card free trial.

- asciinema server from the official image, pinned to 20260626, on one m1.small VM, port 4000.
- Managed Postgres on its own private VM, holding accounts and recording metadata.
- A volume on /var/lib/asciinema, which holds the recording files themselves.
- A public hostname on *.redu.cloud with TLS.

app.start: image pulled from ghcr.io/asciinema/asciinema-server:20260626 (BEAM release, nothing built on the VM)

cost.note: Billed hourly — delete anytime. Egress is usage-based and not included.

app.rule: open 4000 on the app instance's security group (it sits behind the https access point)

database.rule: open 5432 on the managed-postgres security group, reachable from the app's private network ONLY (never public)

ports_and_security_groups.note: Provisioning must apply app, DB, analytics-store, and media rules on the private network as required.

resources.access_point: an auto-generated https://<name>.redu.cloud URL once deployed
resources.private_network: your private network (check_deploy_prerequisites auto-selects your default) — app + DB reachable on it; DB private-only.

warnings: Multi-service compose detected — deploy with deploy_compose (podman-compose on one VM), NOT deploy_app. Pass the EXPOSED service's host port (left side of its `ports:` mapping) + optionally its service name. The stack's own db/redis containers run on the same VM (database:'compose', the default) — only set database:'single_vm'/'managed' if you want a separate redu-managed DB instead, and then your compose must reference DATABASE_URL/PG*/MYSQL_*.

• Make sure the app listens on 0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1/localhost. — #25: redu probes the VM's ROUTABLE interface, and the public proxy maps the domain to floating_ip:PORT. A loopback-bound app can answer on the VM and still 502 for every real visitor. This is the single most common 'deployed but broken' shape and it is stack-independent.

• The app must start on EVERY boot - a container restart policy or a systemd unit. Never a first-boot-only script. — cloud-init runcmd runs on first boot ONLY. A rebooted VM (or a rebuilt cluster member) comes back with nothing running, never rejoins the pool, and silently drains capacity. Measured at 50-60s outages before this was understood.

⚠ This app is told its OWN url (BASE_URL / SITE_URL / callback / hostname env detected). Generate the dname UP FRONT and pass it as `dname`, wiring that exact value into the env - do not let redu auto-generate the URL. — 44 of 46 real deploys carrying env embedded their own redu.cloud URL. redu appends a random 8-char suffix to a bare name, so an auto-generated URL will NOT match anything you wired, and a redeploy changes it again - silently breaking OAuth callbacks and cookies.

• Does this app CREATE its schema on first boot? - "THE SIGN-IN PATH IS /login/new, AND /login IS A 404 ON GET. Learned on deploy #434, because the obvious guess wastes a step. The Explore page links to /login/new; that page's form POSTs to /login with three fields that matter — `_csrf_token` (hidden, 56 chars, must come from the same request as the session cookie) and `login[email]` — plus TWO HONEYPOT FIELDS, `login[username]` (rendered with autocomplete='nope' tabindex='-1') and `login[terms]` (a hidden checkbox). LEAVE BOTH EMPTY/UNCHECKED: filling them is how the app spots a bot. The POST answers 302 whether or not the address is known, deliberately, so the redirect proves nothing about whether a link was generated — read the log. Completing sign-up is a SECOND form: the /users/new?t=... page POSTs to /users with `_csrf_token`, `t` (the same token again, ~116 chars, in a hidden field), `timezone` (filled by JS, so send one yourself, e.g. Europe/London) and `username`. Success is a 302 to /~<username>."
  - "CLOSING SIGNUPS DOES NOT NEED A SECOND deploy_compose. The recipe says 'redeploy with SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true', and a full redeploy builds a NEW VM for a one-word change. What actually works, measured on #434: ssh in, `sudo sed -i 's/^SIGN_UP_DISABLED=.*/SIGN_UP_DISABLED=true/' /opt/app-src/.env`, then `cd /opt/app-src && sudo docker compose up -d`. That recreates the container in seconds; the named volume, the managed database and the pinned URL all survive, and SECRET_KEY_BASE comes from the same .env so nobody is signed out. ALSO change the default in your local compose to `${SIGN_UP_DISABLED:-true}` so a future redeploy cannot reopen signups on an instance whose admin is already claimed. Verify the close from OUTSIDE: POST a stranger address to /login and confirm the log emitted NO new 'url from email' line and `select count(*) from users` is unchanged — the 302 alone tells you nothing."
  - "redu's COMPOSE VM RUNS docker, NOT podman, AND THE PROJECT IS AT /opt/app-src. So it is `sudo docker ...` throughout, the container is named `app-src-<service>-1` (compose project `app-src`, from the upload directory name, NOT your deployment name), and the volume is `app-src_<volume>`. The real environment lives in /opt/app-src/.env, which is where redu appended the managed-DB variables: on #434 that was DATABASE_URL plus PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/[REDACTED:value] and a DATABASE_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/NAME set, alongside APP_URL, PUBLIC_URL and LOGGING_DRIVER that redu adds unasked. The generated password was URL-safe, so the percent-encoding warning above did not bite — but it is one generated password, not a guarantee, so still check."
  - "THERE IS NO psql AND NO /app/bin/asciinema IN THE IMAGE, SO PROVE THE DATABASE FROM A THROWAWAY CONTAINER. `sudo docker exec <container> /app/bin/asciinema eval ...` fails with 'not found'. What works from the VM: `DB=$(sudo docker exec app-src-asciinema-1 printenv DATABASE_URL); sudo docker run --rm postgres:16-alpine psql \"$DB\" -At -c \"select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public' order by 1\"`. On #434 that returned admin_saved_queries, asciicast_daily_views, asciicast_fts, asciicast_stats, asciicasts, clis, oban_jobs, oban_peers, schema_migrations, streams, users — which is what a correctly-wired managed database looks like. Same one-liner confirms the admin claim: `select id, username, email, is_admin from users`."
  - "plan_deploy WILL SIZE THIS AT m1.large AND QUOTE ROUGHLY DOUBLE. Measured on 2026-08-17: it returned m1.large + m1.small at GBP 0.066/hr (GBP 48.18/mo) against the real m1.small + m1.small at GBP 0.0348/hr (GBP 25.40/mo), because needs_compose:true raises the app VM to a 'build-capable floor'. Nothing is built here — the image is pulled — so pass flavor_id '2' explicitly and tell the user the corrected figure, not redu's. plan_deploy's own preflight flags the disagreement with redu.md rather than resolving it, so the override is yours to make."

Deployed and verified.

**https://asciinema-k4m9p2vt.redu.cloud** — deployment #434, `ready`.

- App VM `asciinema` (m1.small) running `ghcr.io/asciinema/asciinema-server:20260626`
- Managed Postgres `db-asciinema` (db #136) on the private network
- **GBP 0.0348/hr, ~GBP 25/month** — redu's sizer wanted m1.large at GBP 48/mo; overridden to m1.small per `redu.md`, and it idles at 173 MiB in a 2 GB VM, so that was right.

**Your admin account is claimed:** user #1, username `milos`, email `«REDACTED:env:013044ef»`, `is_admin = t`. Signups are now closed. The admin panel is at `/admin` behind your login — port 4002, the unauthenticated one, is not published anywhere and times out from outside.

**To sign in** — you have no SMTP, so links go to the container log. There's a fresh one waiting (single-use, expires around 16:45 UTC):

```
https://asciinema-k4m9p2vt.redu.cloud/session/new?t=«REDACTED:urltoken:[REDACTED:value]
```

For future logins:
```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 22025 ubuntu@asciinema-k4m9p2vt.redu.cloud
sudo docker logs app-src-asciinema-1 | grep 'url from email'   # take the LAST one
```

**Point your CLI at it:**
```bash
export ASCIINEMA_SERVER_URL=https://asciinema-k4m9p2vt.redu.cloud   # CLI 3.x
asciinema auth        # links this CLI to your account — required, uploads need auth
asciinema rec demo.cast && asciinema upload demo.cast
```

**Verified, not assumed:** the container's `DATABASE_URL` names `[ip]`, not the `postgres@postgres` the image bakes in, and `users`/`asciicasts`/`schema_migrations` really are in the managed database. Anonymous `POST /api/asciicasts` returns 401. `SECRET_KEY_BASE` was supplied, not regenerated at boot. Only `0.0.0.0:4000` listens on the host.

One correction worth flagging: my first "signups are closed" check omitted a honeypot field in the login form, so the server rejected it as a bot and returned an innocuous 302 that read as a pass. I redid it two-sided — stranger address gets 200 with no link, your address gets 302 with exactly one — and wrote the trap into `redu.md` so it doesn't catch the next run.

**Two things to know:** live streaming is unconfirmed (it needs the edge to pass WebSocket upgrades to `/ws/`; recording and playback don't). And `delete_deployment` destroys the app VM and every `.cast` file with it while the managed Postgres survives holding the metadata and keeps billing — deleting one without the other leaves orphaned data either way.

```

Worth deciding now, since it'll keep coming up: if you'd rather the links actually arrive by email, give me an SMTP relay you already own and I'll add `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` (defaults to 587), `SMTP_USERNAME` and `SMTP_PASSWORD` to `/opt/app-src/.env` and restart the container — about thirty seconds, no redeploy, no data touched. That's also the prerequisite if anyone other than you ever needs an account here, because right now every login requires shell access to the VM.
